newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: NEW NATIONAL ACCOUNTS FIGURES
There's been no suprises in the latest national accounts figures, with a point-five per cent increase in economic growth recorded in the three months to December.
The result translates into an annual rise in average gross domestic product of a respectable three-point-one per cent.
Most of the growth has been generated by private and government consumption, with some from business investment.
The main detraction from growth has come from the import of goods and services.
Among the industry sectors, there's been a decline in manufacturing, while the property, business and mining sectors fared well.
WET CONTINUES IN NORTH-WEST QUEENSLAND
The State Emergency Service is sandbagging buildings around Mt Isa as heavy rain continues to cause problems in the northwestern city.
A house and shed were washed away this morning after their foundations were eroded by floodwaters.
Police are advising landholders futher downstream to start moving belongings .
The SES is sandbagging around the Laura Johnson Old People's Home, with heavy rain causing minor flooding.
It says it's also tarping leaking roofs and there are reports of water starting to seep through concrete slab floors.
OPPOSITION WARNS ON APPOINTMENT OF JUDGES
Deputy Liberal leader Gareth Evans says it's dangerous for a government to appoint new High Court judges in anticipation of them behaving a particular way.
This follows the Deputy Prime Minister's comments that he want's a "Capital-C" conservative judge to replace retiring Chief Justice, Sir Gerard Brenan, next year.
Mr Evans says history is littered with examples of judges being appointed on assumptions about how they'll behave which have back-fired.
A new High Court judge to replace Sir Gerard will be made after consultion with the States.
JURY OUT IN TJANDAMARRA O'SHANE TRIAL
The jury in the trial of the man accused of attempting to murder six-year-old Cairns school boy Tjandamarra O'Shane has retired.
The accused, 27-year-old Paul Wade Streeton has pleaded not guilty to attempted murder, but guilty to grevious bodily harm with intent.
In summing up Crown prosecutor, John Bailey, said the evidence put before the court remained uncontradicted and unchallenged.
He said the point in contest was whether Paul Streeton intended to kill Tjandamarra when he poured petrol on his head an set him alight in the school playground last October.
Defence lawyer Jeremy Darville told the court the accussed didn't set out to kill the boy, and committed the crime to draw attention to himself.
TOP GOVERNMENT JOB FOR MANSFIELD
The Prime Minister has confirmed he's appointed businessman Bob Mansfield as the Government's Major Projects Facilitator.
Mr Mansfield, who recently reviewed the role and responsibilities of the ABC, will be charged with ensuring speedy approval is given to big investment projects.
Mr Howard says Mr Mansfield, who's also the former head of Optus Communications and the Fairfax Newspaper Group, will spend about two to three days a week on the task.
The Prime Minister says he's delighted a businessman of Mr Mansfield's proven experience and status has agreed to perfrom this important new role.
MOTION AGAINST NUCLEAR REPROCESSING PLANT
The Senate is to vote on a motion which calls on the Government to rule out building a nuclear reprocessing plant.
The motion also calls for a commitment to store all of Australia's nuclear waste at its place of manufacture.
The motion was put by Greens Senator by Dee Margetts, following confirmation by the Science Minister that Cabinet's to consider establishing a reprocessing plant at Lucas Heights in Sydney.
The proposal for the plant is one of three options under discussion to solve Australia's future nuclear waste storage problems.
Federal Opposition leader, Kim Beazley, says he doesn't support building a reprocessing plant, but says if it did go ahead, Sydney is definitely not the right location for it.
NEW LOOK FOR TOP F-1 TEAM
One of the greatest teams in the history of Formula-one has made its first public appearance this year, in the lead-up to Sunday's Australian Grand Prix.

Sporting a new look, the McLaren team has departed from its traditional red and white, but insists nothing else will change. Team boss, Ron Dennis gives his drivers a good chance for Sunday's race, but says they'll have to wait a bit longer to guage their chances for the rest of the season.
